data.cultural_impact: The name Ayanaj holds significant cultural influence in Hindu tradition. The root of the name "Ayan" symbolizes the sun god and the dawn of a new day. In Hindu mythology, the sun is considered a source of energy, life, and positivity. Letting the name Ayanaj continue to carry this rich symbolism could inspire those named with the name to embody these qualities - to bring light and sunshine to those around them.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Ayanaj invokes the positive energy of the sun god, representing the rising sun and the promise of a new beginning. The name is deeply rooted in Hindu philosophy and symbolizes enlightenment, progress, and growth. Those named Ayanaj are believed to carry this inner light and shanti, bringing warmth and positivity to those around them.

historical_references.reference: The name Ayanaj is mentioned in the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic poem. It is the name of a king who ruled over the Anga country in the eastern part of India. The Mahabharata was likely composed between 400 BCE and 200 CE.
historical_references.context: Ancient Indian epic poem, Mahabharata, mentions Ayanaj as a king of Anga country.

historical_references.reference: Ayanaj is also mentioned in the Puranas, a set of ancient Indian texts. He is described as a king of Magadha, a kingdom located in the eastern part of India. The Puranas were likely composed between 400 CE and 1200 CE.
